evals.prompt: Spin up a worktree for ENG-4102.
evals.expected_output: The create-worktree skill triggers and runs its full flow: resolve paths, build the branch name, run the bundled script, index CodeGraph, report the result
expectations: Triggers create-worktree rather than answering with a bare `git worktree add` command
Resolves the source repo root with `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` and derives the destination as a sibling directory of the form <repo-basename>-ENG-4102
Fetches the issue title from Linear via mcp__linear__get_issue when only the identifier is supplied, and preserves the identifier casing as ENG-4102
Delegates worktree creation and the `.claude` mirror to scripts/create-worktree.sh rather than emitting inline `git worktree add` / `rm -rf` commands
Runs `codegraph init -i` on the new worktree and reports the file/symbol counts from `codegraph status`
Ends by printing the worktree path, branch, base, and the `cd` + `claude` command without auto-launching a session

evals.expected_output: git-branch-namer produces the branch name only; no worktree, directory, or branch is created
expectations: Does NOT trigger create-worktree — the request is for a name, not an isolated checkout
Routes to git-branch-namer and returns a `prefix/ENG-4102-slug` name in a code block
Creates no directory, runs no `git worktree add`, and runs no CodeGraph indexing

evals.prompt: Make a worktree for ENG-4102 off develop.
evals.expected_output: The create-worktree skill triggers and branches from develop instead of the default main
expectations: Triggers create-worktree and honors `develop` as the base rather than defaulting to `main`
Passes `develop` as the fourth argument to scripts/create-worktree.sh so the worktree is created off `origin/develop`
Reports `origin/develop` as the base in the final summary
Still mirrors `.claude` and indexes CodeGraph — a non-default base changes only the branch point
